differential.name: Atherosclerotic coronary artery disease (subclinical or stable)

supporting_evidence.finding: No statin or other lipid‑lowering therapy documented

differential.reasoning: Severe atherogenic dyslipidaemia together with longstanding hypertension, diabetes, obesity, male sex and age >70 creates a very high pre‑test probability of silent coronary atherosclerosis. The absence of any lipid‑lowering medication further supports that coronary disease is likely present but untreated.

differential.name: Type 2 diabetes mellitus – post‑prandial hyperglycaemia

supporting_evidence.finding: HbA1c 5.6 % (within normal range) – discordant with random glucose
Diagnosed type 2 diabetes (2020) on metformin XR 500 mg
Dyslipidaemia pattern typical of diabetic dyslipidaemia

differential.reasoning: The markedly elevated random glucose despite a normal HbA1c indicates significant post‑prandial spikes or glycaemic variability, a common pattern in older adults on metformin alone. This contributes to the atherogenic lipid profile and overall cardiovascular risk.

differential.name: Primary hypothyroidism

supporting_evidence.finding: Elevated total cholesterol, LDL‑C and triglycerides

differential.reasoning: Hypothyroidism can produce hypercholesterolaemia, hypertriglyceridaemia, mild anaemia and reduced renal potassium excretion. No thyroid function tests are available, making this a plausible but unconfirmed contributor to the metabolic abnormalities.

differential.name: Anemia of chronic disease (mixed with possible iron‑deficiency)

supporting_evidence.finding: Chronic inflammatory load: hypertension, diabetes, metabolic syndrome, chronic sinusitis

differential.reasoning: Long‑standing low‑grade inflammation from metabolic syndrome and chronic sinusitis can suppress iron utilisation, producing anemia of chronic disease. The lack of iron studies leaves a possible iron‑deficiency component, but the available data support ACD as a secondary manifestation of the patient’s systemic disease burden.

primary_diagnosis: Atherosclerotic coronary artery disease (subclinical or stable)
clinical_reasoning_summary: The patient’s profile is dominated by severe atherogenic dyslipidaemia, hypertension, type 2 diabetes, obesity, male sex and advanced age, all of which strongly point to subclinical coronary artery disease as the primary pathology. The discordance between a normal HbA1c and an elevated random glucose indicates post‑prandial hyperglycaemia, which further fuels atherosclerosis. Primary hypothyroidism remains a plausible but less certain contributor to the lipid abnormalities and anemia. Chronic anemia of disease is supported by laboratory data and the patient’s chronic inflammatory milieu, though it is not a driver of the cardiovascular risk.

Current BMI not recorded despite documented obesity

recommended_workup: Fasting lipid panel and calculation of 10‑year ASCVD risk; initiate high‑intensity statin therapy
Coronary artery calcium scoring or pharmacologic stress test to evaluate for subclinical CAD
Fasting plasma glucose and repeat HbA1c; consider 2‑hour oral glucose tolerance test or continuous glucose monitoring for post‑prandial assessment
Thyroid panel (TSH, free T4) to rule in/out hypothyroidism
Comprehensive iron studies (serum ferritin, transferrin saturation), vitamin B12, folate, and fecal occult blood test or colonoscopy to investigate anemia
Repeat serum potassium with review of ACE‑inhibitor dose; dietary potassium counseling if needed
Basic metabolic panel with repeat eGFR to confirm renal function stability
Transthoracic echocardiogram with diastolic function parameters and NT‑proBNP to assess for HFpEF
Ankle‑brachial index and lower‑extremity duplex ultrasound to screen for PAD
STOP‑BANG questionnaire followed by overnight polysomnography if high risk for obstructive sleep apnoea
Social work referral for housing stability and PHQ‑9 depression screening
